amoled.blurb: adds an AMOLED target, with a sparse always-on sleep frame
amoled.text:
# A face that also targets an AMOLED watch, with an always-on sleep frame.
#
# An AMOLED screen that stayed on all day would burn in, so while the watch
# sleeps it draws a separate, sparse frame instead (docs/guide/always-on-display.md).
# You don't write a second design: `aod:` on an element is a block of
# overrides for that frame (writing one also shows it; `visible: false`
# hides it), and `defaults: {aod: ...}` below is the same block for every
# element that says nothing.
#
# Here everything is hidden asleep except the clock, drawn as a thin outline
# around black digits, and a dimmer, thinner battery ring. `dim:` scales every
# colour the sleep frame draws; the clock's own `dim: 1` keeps its outline
# at full brightness. A moving pixel mask is on by default, so no pixel
# stays lit two minutes running.
#
# The MIP watches in `targets:` are always on already and ignore `aod:`.
#
# Preview the sleep frame with:  wfb preview <file> -d fenix847mm --aod
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix847mm, fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
defaults:
  aod:
    visible: false
    dim: 0.6

resources:
  palette:
    black: "#000000"
    white: "#FFFFFF"
    gray: "#AAAAAA"
    dark: "#555555"
    accent: "#00AAFF"
    hot: "#FF5500"

elements:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.black

  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d %b}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -36%r }
    color: color.gray

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center }
    color: color.white
    aod:
      dim: 1
      color: color.black   # hollow digits: only the outline lights
      outline:
        width: 2
        color: color.gray

  heart:
    type: group
    size: { width: 30%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 38%r }
    on_hold: heart_rate
    children:
      hr_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: heart
        size: 10%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.hot
      hr_value:
        type: text
        text: "{heart_rate.current:d}"
        font: FONT_TINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 13%r }
        align: left
        color: color.white
        absent: "--"

  battery_ring:
    type: gauge
    style: arc
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 90%r
    thickness: 3%r
    start_angle: 210deg
    sweep: 300deg
    color: color.accent
    track_color: color.dark
    aod:
      thickness: 1%r
      color: color.dark

analog.blurb: a three-hand dial with ticks, numerals and a date window
analog.text:
# A classic three-hand dial: minute and hour ticks, twelve numerals, a date
# window at 3 o'clock, and hour, minute and second hands.
#
# The dial -- ticks, numerals, the window's frame -- never changes, so it sits
# in `static:` and is painted once into a buffer rather than every second.
#
# A hand is drawn pointing at 12 o'clock in a frame whose origin is its axis
# (docs/guide/analog-hands.md); the watch turns it. `dy` is negative towards
# the tip. The second hand vanishes while the watch sleeps (`seconds: awake`,
# the default) -- a MIP face redraws only once a minute then.
#
# Preview a flattering time with:  wfb preview <file> --time 10:09:42
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"
    accent: "#FF5500"

  hand_sets:
    classic:
      hour:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - type: polygon
            points:
              - { dx: -3%r, dy: 8%r } # a short tail behind the axis
              - { dx: -2%r, dy: -40%r }
              - { dy: -46%r } # the tip
              - { dx: 2%r, dy: -40%r }
              - { dx: 3%r, dy: 8%r }
      minute:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - { type: rectangle, at: { dy: -32%r }, size: { width: 3%r, height: 76%r } }
      second:
        color: color.accent
        parts:
          - { type: line, at: { dy: 15%r }, to: { dy: -84%r }, thickness: 2px }
          - { type: circle, at: { dy: 15%r }, radius: 3%r }  # counterweight

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

  minute_ticks:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center } # the point every copy turns about
    count: 60 # step defaults to 360deg / 60 = 6deg
    skip_every: 5 # leave the hour positions to hour_ticks
    color: color.dim
    parts: # copy 0, as it looks at 12 o'clock
      - { type: line, at: { dy: -96%r }, to: { dy: -90%r }, thickness: 1px }

  hour_ticks:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center }
    count: 12
    color: color.fg
    parts:
      - { type: rectangle, at: { dy: -90%r }, size: { width: 3%r, height: 10%r } }

  # One radial pattern instead of twelve text elements. `copy` is the copy's
  # index, 0 at 12 o'clock, so this draws 12, 1, 2, ... 11. The 3 is skipped:
  # the date window sits there.
  numerals:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center }
    count: 12
    skip: [3]
    color: color.dim
    parts:
      - type: text
        text: "{(copy + 11) % 12 + 1}"
        font: FONT_SMALL
        at: { dy: -70%r }

  date_frame:
    type: rectangle
    filled: false
    thickness: 1px
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 62%r }
    size: { width: 26%r, height: 18%r }
    color: color.dim

elements:
  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.day:d}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 62%r }
    color: color.fg

  hands:
    type: hands
    set: classic
    at: { anchor: center }
  pin:
    type: circle
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 3%r
    color: color.accent

calendar.blurb: the time over a Monday-first month of dots, today lit
calendar.text:
# The time over a month at a glance: a Monday-first calendar of dots, today
# lit and the days already gone dimmed, under a row of weekday initials.
#
# Both are `pattern: grid` -- one template repeated in rows of `columns:`.
# Inside a pattern, `copy` is the index of the copy being drawn (0, 1, 2 ...),
# so a colour, a text part or a part's `visible:` can differ per copy
# (docs/guide/patterns.md "Grids").
#
# The grid has 37 cells -- enough for a 31-day month starting on a Sunday.
# `first` below is the column the 1st falls in, worked out from today's
# weekday and date (`date.weekday` is 1 for Sunday, so `+ 5` makes Monday
# column 0; the `+ 35` keeps the `%` operand positive). The cells before it
# are hidden. A pattern cannot know the month's length, so a short month
# still draws 31 dots: the last ones simply never light.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    past: "#AAAAAA"
    today: "#FFAA00"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

  # Reads only `copy`, so it never changes and can live in `static:`.
  weekdays:
    type: pattern
    pattern: grid
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -42%r, dy: -14%r } # copy 0's place
    count: 7
    columns: 7
    step: { dx: 14%r }
    color: color.past
    parts:
      - type: text
        text: >-
          {(copy == 0 ? "M" : copy == 1 ? "T" : copy == 2 ? "W" : copy == 3 ? "T" :
          copy == 4 ? "F" : copy == 5 ? "S" : "S")}
        font: FONT_XTINY

elements:
  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_MEDIUM
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -54%r }
    color: color.fg

  month:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%b %Y}"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -30%r }
    color: color.today

  # first = (date.weekday + 5 - (date.day - 1) + 35) % 7, written out inline:
  # a pattern expression cannot name an intermediate value.
  days:
    type: pattern
    pattern: grid
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -42%r, dy: -2%r }
    count: 37
    columns: 7
    step: { dx: 14%r, dy: 11%r }
    color: >-
      copy == (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 + date.day - 1 ? color.today : (copy < (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 + date.day - 1 ? color.past : color.fg)
    parts:
      - type: circle
        radius: 3%r
        visible: "copy >= (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 && copy < (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 + 31"

dashboard.blurb: time, a goal ring, two data clusters and a battery bar
dashboard.text:
# A denser starting point: the time, a goal ring, two data clusters and battery.
#
# Offsets are in %r -- percentages of the screen's minor radius -- so the design
# keeps its proportions on both the 260x260 and 280x280 families rather than
# drifting. Use %r for anything you think of as "this far out from the middle".
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    text: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"
    accent: "#00AAFF"
    hot: "#FF5500"
    track: "#555555"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

elements:
  # A stroked ring, open at the bottom. There is no filled-sector primitive in
  # Connect IQ, so `thickness` is a pen width and there is no inner radius.
  step_ring:
    type: gauge
    style: arc
    value: activity.steps
    max: activity.step_goal
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 88%r
    thickness: 9px
    start_angle: 215deg # measured clockwise from 12 o'clock
    sweep: 290deg
    color: color.accent
    track_color: color.track
    absent: hide      # required: both bindings can be absent

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -12%r }
    color: color.text

  hr_icon:
    type: icon
    icon: heart
    size: 11%r
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -40%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.hot

  hr_value:
    type: text
    text: "{heart_rate.current:d}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -17%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.text
    absent: "--"

  steps_icon:
    type: icon
    icon: steps
    size: 11%r
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 13%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.accent

  steps_value:
    type: text
    text: "{activity.steps / 1000:.01f}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 38%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.text
    absent: "--"

  battery:
    type: gauge
    style: bar
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 62%r }
    size: { width: 40%r, height: 5%r }
    color: color.text
    track_color: color.track

gauge.blurb: a battery needle gauge over the top half, the time below it
gauge.text:
# An instrument-style face: a battery gauge across the top half, its needle
# turning from E at 9 o'clock to F at 3, and the time below the axis, where
# the needle never goes.
#
# A needle (`gauge` with `style: needle`) is authored like an analog
# hand -- its parts point at 12 o'clock, in a frame whose origin is the axis
# -- and turns to `start_angle + value / max x sweep`, clockwise from 12
# (docs/guide/progress-and-graphs.md "Gauge needles"). The tick ring is a
# radial `pattern` sharing the needle's start angle and sweep: 11 ticks
# 18 degrees apart span the same 180 degrees.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    scale: "#AAAAAA"
    accent: "#FFAA00"
    low: "#FF0000"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

  battery_ticks:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center }
    count: 11
    start: 270deg
    step: 18deg
    color: color.scale
    parts:
      - { type: line, at: { dy: -94%r }, to: { dy: -84%r }, thickness: 2px }

  empty_mark:
    type: text
    text: "E"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -76%r, dy: 12%r }
    color: color.low

  full_mark:
    type: text
    text: "F"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 76%r, dy: 12%r }
    color: color.scale

elements:
  # A colour may read data: the needle turns red below 20%. Parts without a
  # colour of their own take the element's.
  battery_needle:
    type: gauge
    style: needle
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center }
    start_angle: 270deg
    sweep: 180deg
    color: "system.battery < 20 ? color.low : color.accent"
    needle:
      - type: polygon
        points: [{ dx: -3%r, dy: 10%r }, { dx: -1%r, dy: -74%r },  dy: -80%r, { dx: 1%r, dy: -74%r }, { dx: 3%r, dy: 10%r }]
      - { type: circle, radius: 6%r, color: color.fg }    # the hub, drawn last

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_MEDIUM
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 38%r }
    color: color.fg

  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d}"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 64%r }
    color: color.scale

minimal.blurb: a background and the time -- the smallest face worth building
minimal.text:
# The smallest face worth building: a background and the time.
#
# Everything here uses a system font, so this design needs no asset files at all.
# To use your own typeface, add a `fonts:` block and point an element at it:
#
#   fonts:
#     clock:
#       source: assets/YourFont.ttf
#       size: 18%r          # of this device's minor radius (px and %r only)
#
#   ...then `font: font.clock` on the text element.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]

# Every channel is 0x00, 0x55, 0xAA or 0xFF -- the only values a 64-colour MIP
# panel shows without dithering. The linter checks this.
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    text: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

elements:
  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    # %h follows the watch's own 12/24-hour setting, which %H and %I do not.
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center }
    color: color.text

  seconds:
    type: text
    text: "{time.second:02d}"
    font: FONT_SMALL
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.dim

navy_classic.blurb: a navy sunray dress dial: polygon hands, batons, a day/date window at 3

palette.blurb: all 64 MIP colours as named swatches, with a colour scheme and colour axes

showcase.blurb: three layouts switched by Styles -- a classic analog dial, a dense digital dashboard, and a vintage roman dial
showcase.text:
# Showcase -- one face, three layouts switched by Styles: `analog` (a quiet
# three-hand dial with tick and numeral patterns), `digital` (a dense
# dashboard: two-tone clock, weather row, heart-rate graph, data clusters,
# gauge bar and ring, status row), and `roman` (a vintage roman-numeral
# dial with Breguet-style hands and a mechanical day/date aperture). Two
# shared
# `data` element registers draw beneath all three.
#
# Config: several colour schemes paired with the layouts as `config: style:`
# entries, both colour axes, and the Data axis (the two registers). fr955
# has no native editor, so it offers them from the generated settings menu.
#
# Preview it:  wfb preview <file> --all-styles
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets:
    - fenix8solar47mm
    - fenix8solar51mm
    - fr955

resources:
  fonts:
    digitalclock:
      source: assets/ChivoMono-Bold.ttf
      size: 60%r
      monospace: true
      align: center
      antialias: true
    dialfont:
      source: assets/Dynalight-Regular.ttf
      size: 13%r
      antialias: true
    # Device-resident, scalable -- `docs/guide/fonts.md` "Vector (`face:`) fonts".
    # RobotoCondensedBold is the one Latin face all three targets publish
    # (checked against each device's `scalable_faces`), so this needs no
    # `unsupported:` -- the roman layout's numeral ring turns it with
    # `curve:`, which only a `face:` font can do (a baked sheet cannot rotate).
    romandial:
      # face: [RobotoCondensedBold]
      face: [RobotoCondensedRegular]
      size: 32%r

  palette:
    black: { value: "#000000", label: "Black" }
    white: { value: "#FFFFFF", label: "White" }
    light_gray: { value: "#AAAAAA", label: "Light Gray" }
    dark_gray: { value: "#555555", label: "Dark Gray" }
    darkest_blue: { value: "#000055", label: "Midnight" }
    red: { value: "#FF0000", label: "Red" }
    orange: { value: "#FF5500", label: "Orange" }
    amber: { value: "#FFAA00", label: "Amber" }
    yellow: { value: "#FFFF00", label: "Yellow" }
    green: { value: "#00FF00", label: "Green" }
    lime_green: { value: "#AAFF00", label: "Lime Green" }
    cyan: { value: "#00FFFF", label: "Cyan" }
    sky_blue: { value: "#00AAFF", label: "Sky Blue" }
    light_blue: { value: "#55FFFF", label: "Light Blue" }
    magenta: { value: "#FF00FF", label: "Magenta" }
    dark_green: { value: "#005500", label: "Dark Green" }
    dark_red: { value: "#550000", label: "Dark Red" }

  # One named hand set, authored pointing at 12 o'clock, origin = the axis
  # (docs/guide/analog-hands.md). Tapered hour/minute polygons plus a
  # needle-thin second hand whose tip is the one native accent-colour axis.
  hand_sets:
    classic:
      hour:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - type: polygon
            points:
              - { dx: -3%r, dy: 8%r }
              - { dx: -2%r, dy: -38%r }
              - { dy: -46%r }
              - { dx: 2%r, dy: -38%r }
              - { dx: 3%r, dy: 8%r }
      minute:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - { type: rectangle, at: { dy: -34%r }, size: { width: 3%r, height: 78%r } }
          - { type: circle, radius: 4%r }
      second:
        color: color.dim
        parts:
          - { type: line, at: { dy: 14%r }, to: { dy: -76%r }, thickness: 1px }
          - { type: circle, at: { dy: 14%r }, radius: 3%r }
          - { type: circle, radius: 2%r, color: color.accent }
          - { type: line, at: { dy: -76%r }, to: { dy: -64%r }, thickness: 2px, color: color.accent }

  # A second hand set for the roman layout -- `classic` above is untouched,
  # since the analog layout still uses it. "Vintage" here means Breguet
  # (moon) hour/minute hands: a tapered shaft, an open ring set near the tip,
  # and a short point beyond it -- the read a period dress watch's hands
  # give -- without inventing any part kind a hand does not already have
  # (`docs/guide/analog-hands.md` -- polygon/rectangle/line/circle only).
  # The hour hand is both shorter AND visibly heavier (a 4%r-wide shaft
  # against the minute's 2.4%r) than the minute hand, and
  # both stay clear of the numeral ring, which starts well past the minute
  # hand's -64%r tip.
  #
  # Revised after rendering `--style roman_crimson --time 4:38:12` showed a
  # visible gap at the hub: the first draft's shaft tails were too thin to
  # read as "meeting" anything, and a separate `color.bg` pin
  # (`roman_center_pin`, drawn last, over every hand) was punching a hole
  # bigger than those thin tails -- fine on `classic`'s much thicker hands
  # (a deliberate "drilled screw" look there), but on these it erased the
  # joint, and the second hand's own accent-coloured pivot jewel, instead
  # of covering it. `docs/guide/analog-hands.md`'s own idiom for this ("a hub *between*
  # hands is a circle part at the origin of the hand below it") is what
  # `classic`'s `minute` already does -- a plain filled circle at the
  # origin, drawn as part of `minute` so it sits over `hour`'s shaft below
  # it. `vintage` now does the same, sized to comfortably cover the
  # thicker shafts below: `minute`'s own hub circle (`radius: 3%r`) covers
  # the `hour`/`minute` joint, and `second` (drawn last, per the fixed
  # hour/minute/second order) rides on top of that with its own small
  # accent-coloured pivot dot as the jewel at dead centre -- no separate
  # trailing pin element needed, so `roman_center_pin` is gone.
    vintage:
      hour:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          # bg
          - type: polygon                     # tapered shaft, heavier than the minute's
            color: color.black
            points:
              - { dx: -3%r, dy: 11%r }         # a short tail past the axis
              - { dx: -2.5%r, dy: -27%r }
              - { dx: 2.5%r, dy: -27%r }
              - { dx: 3%r, dy: 11%r }
          - type: circle                       # the open "moon" ring -- bigger, chunkier
            color: color.black
            at: { dy: -32%r }
            radius: 5%r
            filled: false
            thickness: 4px
          - type: polygon                      # the point beyond the ring
            color: color.black
            points:
              - { dx: -2.5%r, dy: -35%r }
              - { dy: -42%r }
              - { dx: 2.5%r, dy: -35%r }
        # fg
          - type: polygon                     # tapered shaft, heavier than the minute's
            points:
              - { dx: -2%r, dy: 10%r }         # a short tail past the axis
              - { dx: -1.5%r, dy: -26%r }
              - { dx: 1.5%r, dy: -26%r }
              - { dx: 2%r, dy: 10%r }
          - type: circle                       # the open "moon" ring -- bigger, chunkier
            at: { dy: -32%r }
            radius: 4%r
            filled: false
            thickness: 2px
          - type: polygon                      # the point beyond the ring
            points:
              - { dx: -1.5%r, dy: -34%r }
              - { dy: -40%r }
              - { dx: 1.5%r, dy: -34%r }
      minute:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          # bg
          - type: circle                       # the hub: covers the hour/minute joint
            color: color.black
            radius: 4%r                        # `at:` defaults to the axis
          - type: polygon
            color: color.black
            points:
              - { dx: -2.2%r, dy: 13%r }        # a longer tail than the hour's --
              - { dx: -2%r, dy: -45%r }         # the counterweight below reads as its mass
              - { dx: 2%r, dy: -45%r }
              - { dx: 2.2%r, dy: 13%r }
          - type: circle                       # a small counterweight, past the axis
            color: color.black
            at: { dy: 12%r }
            radius: 3%r
          - type: circle                       # the open "moon" ring -- bigger, chunkier
            color: color.black
            at: { dy: -52%r }
            radius: 5.5%r
            filled: false
            thickness: 4px
          - type: polygon                      # the point beyond the ring
            color: color.black
            points:
              - { dx: -2%r, dy: -55%r }
              - { dy: -66%r }
              - { dx: 2%r, dy: -55%r }
        # fg
          - type: circle                       # the hub: covers the hour/minute joint
            radius: 3%r                        # `at:` defaults to the axis
          - type: polygon
            points:
              - { dx: -1.2%r, dy: 12%r }        # a longer tail than the hour's --
              - { dx: -1%r, dy: -44%r }         # the counterweight below reads as its mass
              - { dx: 1%r, dy: -44%r }
              - { dx: 1.2%r, dy: 12%r }
          - type: circle                       # a small counterweight, past the axis
            at: { dy: 12%r }
            radius: 2%r
          - type: circle                       # the open "moon" ring -- bigger, chunkier
            at: { dy: -52%r }
            radius: 4.5%r
            filled: false
            thickness: 2px
          - type: polygon                      # the point beyond the ring
            points:
              - { dx: -1%r, dy: -54%r }
              - { dy: -64%r }
              - { dx: 1%r, dy: -54%r }
      second:
        # A thin needle with a counterweight tail, same convention as
        # `classic`'s own second hand (R2.4): color.accent at the tip,
        # `seconds: awake` on the element so the sleeping frame drops it. Its
        # own small circle at the axis (radius 1.5%r, accent-coloured) is the
        # final pivot jewel, riding on top of `minute`'s wider hub circle
        # above -- the last thing drawn, dead centre.
        # color: color.dim
        color: color.accent
        parts:
          - { type: line, at: { dy: 16%r }, to: { dy: -72%r }, thickness: 1px }
          - { type: circle, at: { dy: 16%r }, radius: 2.5%r }
          - { type: circle, radius: 1.5%r, color: color.accent }
        # - { type: line, at: { dy: -72%r }, to: { dy: -62%r }, thickness: 1px, color: color.accent }

# Shared: drawn underneath every layout, roman included -- two side

theme:

config:

static:

elements:
  left_register:
    type: data
    slot: left_register
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -50%r, dy: -30%r }
    font: FONT_XTINY
    icon: { size: 9%r, position: top, gap: 1%r, color: color.data }
    color: color.fg
    label: none
    absent: "--"
    on_hold: auto
    lint:
      allow: [static-overlap]
      reason: "Both the analog layout's full-dial tick/numeral patterns and
        the roman layout's own numeral ring bound this register card's overlap
        box (any dynamic element trivially overlaps a full-circle pattern's
        bounding disc). Analog's numerals (radius 78%r, the small
        font.dialfont) clear this card with a visible gap, confirmed by
        rendering `--time 10:09:30` -- 'X' and '2' sit above it, not inside
        it. Roman's own ring (radius 69%r, the much larger font.romandial) is
        a different story: II and X land almost exactly on this register's
        position (`dx: ±50%r, dy: -30%r` is ~58%r out at ~59° off 12, i.e. the
        2/10 o'clock spokes -- a `complication_slot` cannot live inside a
        `layouts:` body, so this position is fixed for every layout) and DID
        draw under the card and its icon before the roman `numerals` pattern
        below added `skip: [2, 10]` for exactly this reason. With the skip in
        place, no roman numeral's ink falls inside this card either --
        re-checked the same way, at the same time, on all three targets, after
        the skip"

  right_register:
    type: data
    slot: right_register
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 50%r, dy: -30%r }
    font: FONT_XTINY
    icon: { size: 9%r, position: top, gap: 1%r, color: color.data }
    color: color.fg
    label: none
    # `choices: any`: weather conditions and training status get their
    # 7-character names, so they stay inside this small register.
    short: true
    absent: "--"
    lint:
      allow: [static-overlap]
      reason: "Same full-dial-pattern bounding-box overstatement as
        left_register above (both analog's and roman's numeral rings, roman's
        own only true after `skip: [2, 10]` -- see that reason), mirrored at
        dx +42%r"

layouts:
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Analog: a classic three-hand dial. Quiet on purpose -- the two shared
  # registers above are its only readings.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  analog:
    static:
      dial_ring:
        type: arc
        at: { anchor: center }
        radius: 94%r
        thickness: 2px
        start_angle: 0deg
        sweep: 360deg
        color: color.track

      minute_ticks:
        type: pattern
        pattern: radial
        at: { anchor: center }
        count: 60
        skip_every: 5
        color: color.track
        antialias: true
        lint:
          allow: [antialias-dither]
          reason: "a soft edge on the 64-colour MIP panel dithers; accepted
            so the turned ticks do not stair-step -- reported against this
            element, the first to draw anti-aliased, for the whole device"
        parts:
          - { type: line, at: { dy: -90%r }, to: { dy: -86%r }, thickness: 1px }

      hour_ticks:
        type: pattern
        pattern: radial
        at: { anchor: center }
        count: 12
        step: 30deg
        color: color.fg
        antialias: true
        parts:
          - { type: rectangle, at: { dy: -87%r }, size: { width: 2%r, height: 6%r } }

      # Twelve numerals as one radial `type: text` pattern part, rather
      # than twelve polar `text` elements (docs/guide/patterns.md "Text parts").
      hour_numerals:
        type: pattern
        pattern: radial
        at: { anchor: center }
        count: 12
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - type: text
            text: "{(copy + 11) % 12 + 1}"
            font: font.dialfont
            at: { dy: -78%r }

      bottom_card:
        type: rectangle
        at: { anchor: center, dy: 30%r }
        size: { width: 42%r, height: 19%r }
        corner_radius: 3%r
        color: color.dark

      bottom_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: "U+E241"
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: center, dy: 45%r }
        color: color.data




    elements:
      bottom_data:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.steps / 1000.0:.1f}k" # always one decimal, so the width holds still
        # text: "{complication.steps}"
        at: { anchor: center, dy: 30%r }
        font: FONT_XTINY
        # icon: { size: 9%r, position: top, gap: 1%r, color: color.data }
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

      top_data:
        type: group
        at: { anchor: center, dy: -20% }
        size: { width: 25%, height: 25% }
        # visible: device.notification_count > 0
        children:
          top_icon_bg:
            type: icon
            icon: notification
            size: 25%r
            at: { anchor: center, dx: 1%r, dy: 1%r }
            color: color.black
          top_icon:
            type: icon
            icon: notification
            size: 25%r
            at: { anchor: center }
            color: color.track
          top_text_bg:
            type: text
            text: "{device.notification_count:d}"
            font: FONT_TINY
            at: { anchor: center, dx: -1%r, dy: -3%r }
            color: color.black
          top_text:
            type: text
            text: "{device.notification_count:d}"
            font: FONT_TINY
            at: { anchor: center, dy: -2%r }
            color: color.bg

      analog_hands:
        type: hands
        set: classic
        at: { anchor: center }
        seconds: awake
        antialias: true
        lint:
          allow: [antialias-dither]
          reason: "a soft edge on the 64-colour MIP panel dithers; accepted
            so the rotated hands do not stair-step"

      center_pin:
        type: circle
        at: { anchor: center }
        radius: 3%r
        color: color.bg

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Digital: dense and data-rich.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  digital:
    static:
      sep_top:
        type: line
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 24%, dx: 38% }
        to: { anchor: top, dy: 24%, dx: -38% }
        thickness: 1px
        color: color.dark
        lint:
          allow: [contrast]
          reason: "a hairline rule is meant to be barely there; full contrast
            would make it compete with the data around it"

      # sep_bottom:
      #   type: line
      #   at: { anchor: bottom, dy: -20%, dx: 33% }
      #   to: { anchor: bottom, dy: -20%, dx: -33% }
      #   thickness: 1px
      #   color: color.dark
      #   lint:
      #     allow: [contrast]
      #     reason: "a hairline rule is meant to be barely there; full contrast
      #       would make it compete with the data around it"

    elements:
      date_line:
        type: text
        text: "{date.today:%a, %e %b}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 10% }
        color: color.dim

      weather_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: { for: weather.condition_today }
        size: 16%r
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 20% }
        color: color.fg

      # `weather.*` has no documented value range in the catalogue, so the
      # text-overflow lint sizes its box from the format's conservative
      # 5-digit fallback ("88888°", `ts/src/formatting.ts`'s `DEFAULT_DIGITS`)
      # rather than a realistic temperature -- centring it, rather than
      # offsetting it with `dx:`, keeps that oversized box symmetric and
      # well inside the round bezel regardless.
      weather_now:
        type: text
        text: "{weather.feels_like_temperature:d}°"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 20%, dx: -10% }
        align: center
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--°"
        lint:
          allow: [text-overflow]
          reason: "weather.feels_like_temperature has no documented range, so
            the lint's fallback assumes 5 digits ('88888°'); a real reading
            is 1-3 digits and this box is centred with wide margin either
            side of it"

      hr_graph_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: "U+F21E"
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 30% }
        align: center
        color: color.data

      center_card:
        type: rectangle
        at: { anchor: center, dy: -23%r }
        size: { width: 54%r, height: 19%r }
        corner_radius: 3%r
        color: color.dark

      hr_graph:
        type: graph
        series: heart_rate
        range: 4h
        style: area
        at: { anchor: center, dy: -23%r }
        size: { width: 52%r, height: 17%r }
        min: auto
        max: auto
        color: color.data
        on_hold: heart_rate

      hours:
        type: text
        text: "{time.hour:02d}"
        font: font.digitalclock
        at: { anchor: center, dx: -1%, dy: 7% }
        align: right
        color: color.fg

      minutes:
        type: text
        text: "{time.minute:02d}"
        font: font.digitalclock
        at: { anchor: center, dx: 1%, dy: 7% }
        align: left
        color: color.accent

      bb_cluster:
        type: group
        size: { width: 26%r, height: 11%r }
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 75%, dx: -27% }
        align: left
        on_hold: body_battery
        children:
          hr_icon:
            type: icon
            icon: body_battery
            size: 9%r
            color: color.fg
            # at: { anchor: center, dx: -30% }
            at: { anchor: left }
          hr_value:
            type: text
            text: "{complication.body_battery:d}"
            font: FONT_XTINY
            # at: { anchor: center, dx: 25% }
            at: { anchor: left, dx: 14%r }
            color: color.fg
            absent: "--"

      steps_cluster:
        type: group
        size: { width: 38%r, height: 12%r }
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 75% }
        on_hold: steps
        children:
          steps_icon:
            type: icon
            icon: steps
            size: 9%r
            color: color.fg
            # at: { anchor: center, dx: -10%r }
            at: { anchor: left }
            align: left
          steps_value:
            type: text
            text: "{activity.steps / 1000.0:.1f}k"
            font: FONT_XTINY
            # at: { anchor: center, dx: 15%r }
            at: { anchor: left, dx: 13%r }
            align: left
            color: color.fg
            absent: "--"

      calories_cluster:
        type: group
        size: { width: 25%r, height: 12%r }
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 75%, dx: 27% }
        on_hold: calories
        align: right
        children:
          calories_icon:
            type: icon
            icon: flame
            size: 9%r
            color: color.fg
            # at: { anchor: center, dx: -30% }
            at: { anchor: left }
            align: left
          calories_value:
            type: text
            text: "{activity.calories:d}"
            font: FONT_XTINY
            # at: { anchor: center, dx: 30% }
            at: { anchor: left, dx: 10%r }
            align: left
            color: color.fg
            absent: "--"

      steps_bar:
        type: gauge
        style: bar
        value: activity.steps
        max: activity.step_goal
        at: { anchor: top, dy: 82% }
        size: { width: 60%, height: 3%r }
        color: color.accent
        track_color: color.dark
        absent: hide

      battery_arc_l:
        type: gauge
        style: arc
        value: system.battery
        max: 100
        at: { anchor: center }
        radius: 97%r
        thickness: 3%r
        start_angle: 180deg
        sweep: 30deg
        color: color.data
        track_color: color.dark
        lint:
          allow: [safe-area]
          reason: "hugs the bezel by design, the same as a real chronograph's
            outer track -- the pen straddles the round display's own edge
            mask at this radius on every target"

      battery_arc_r:
        type: gauge
        style: arc
        value: system.battery
        max: 100
        at: { anchor: center }
        radius: 97%r
        thickness: 3%r
        start_angle: 180deg
        sweep: -30deg
        color: color.data
        track_color: color.dark
        lint:
          allow: [safe-area]
          reason: "hugs the bezel by design, the same as a real chronograph's
            outer track -- the pen straddles the round display's own edge
            mask at this radius on every target"

      charging_bolt:
        type: icon
        # icon: battery
        icon: "U+F140B"
        size: 12%r
        at: { anchor: bottom, dy: -11%, dx: -18% }
        color: color.accent
        visible: system.charging
        lint:
          allow: [safe-area]
          reason: "sits on the same bezel-hugging arc as battery_arc, for
            the same reason"

      dnd_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: dnd
        size: 12%r
        at: { anchor: bottom, dy: -11%, dx: -12% }
        color: "device.do_not_disturb ? color.accent : color.dark"

      notification_badge:
        type: icon
        icon: notification
        size: 25%r
        at: { anchor: bottom, dy: -10% }
        color: "device.notification_count > 0 ? color.accent : color.dark"

      notification_count:
        type: text
        text: "{device.notification_count:d}"
        font: FONT_TINY
        at: { anchor: bottom, dy: -11% }
        visible: device.notification_count > 0
        color: color.notify

      alarm_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: alarm
        size: 12%r
        at: { anchor: bottom, dy: -11%, dx: 12% }
        color: "device.alarm_count > 0 ? color.accent : color.dark"

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Roman: a classy, vintage dial. Big roman numerals curved
  # around the rim (with II and X given up to the two shared registers,
  # which read as sub-dials at 2 and 10 o'clock -- see `skip:` below),
  # Breguet-style hands (see `hand_sets: vintage:` above), and a
  # mechanical-looking day/date aperture above and below the axle.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  roman:
    static:
      # Twelve numerals as one radial `type: text` pattern part, the same
      # device-resident-font route `analog`'s own `hour_numerals` uses for
      # plain digits (docs/guide/patterns.md "Text parts") -- except this one turns
      # each numeral with `curve:` so its own bottom faces the centre
      # (level at XII, on its side at III/IX, inverted at VI), which only a
      # `face:` (vector) font can do; a baked sheet cannot rotate at all
      # (root CLAUDE.md constraint 15). The chained ternary over `copy` is
      # how a roman numeral is picked: the expression language has string
      # literals and nested ternaries, no arrays or lookup tables
      # (`ts/src/expr.ts`) -- verbose on purpose, reads as a table.
      #
      # Size and radius (26%r, -69%r) were tuned by rendering, not
      # asserted: a first try (22%r/-78%r)
      # tripped `safe-area` on fenix8solar47mm and fr955 because the ring's
      # ink reached past the round panel's own visible disc
      # (`BEZEL_MARGIN` in `ts/src/layout.ts`, a 2% inset). 26%r/-69%r is
      # warning-free on all three targets and reads as big and vintage
      # rather than cramped; the minute hand's own tip (-64%r, `hand_sets:
      # vintage:` below) sits just inside the ring's inner edge, which is
      # deliberate -- a real dress watch's hands do pass close beneath the
      # chapter ring.
      # `skip: [2, 10]` leaves out II and X. This is not decoration -- a
      # `data` element cannot appear inside a `layouts:` body
      # (docs/guide/configuration.md), so the two shared registers are fixed at
      # `dx: ±50%r, dy: -30%r` for every layout, which resolves to ~58%r
      # from the axis at ~59° either side of 12 -- almost exactly where II
      # and X land on a 12-count ring. Rendered without the skip, the
      # register cards and their icons drew right on top of both glyphs
      # (confirmed by rendering `--time 10:09:30` and looking at 2 and 10
      # o'clock, not assumed). Letting a sub-dial or window displace the
      # numeral it would otherwise collide with is period-correct -- a
      # date window replacing III at 3 o'clock is the textbook case -- so
      # the two registers now read as a pair of vintage sub-dials sitting
      # where II and X would have been, rather than numerals fighting
      # complications for the same few square millimetres.
      numerals:
        type: pattern
        pattern: radial
        at: { anchor: center }
        count: 12
        # skip: [2, 10]
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - type: text
            text: >-
              {(copy == 0 ? "XII" : copy == 1 ? "I"   : copy == 2 ? "II" :
              copy == 3 ? "III" : copy == 4 ? "IV"  : copy == 5 ? "V" :
              copy == 6 ? "VI"  : copy == 7 ? "VII" : copy == 8 ? "VIII" :
              copy == 9 ? "IX" : copy == 10 ? "X" : "XI")}
            font: font.romandial
            # at: { dy: -69%r }
            # curve: { style: angled, angle: 0deg }
            curve: { style: radial, angle: 0deg, radius: 80%r }
            align: bottom
        lint:
          allow: [off-screen]
          reason: "big roman numerals run to the rim on purpose, like a dress
            watch's chapter ring; the glyphs' outer edge meets the round screen
            edge by design, and the device clips the few pixels past it"

      # A "mechanical opening" without alpha:
      # `alphaBlendingSupport` is false on every target (root CLAUDE.md
      # constraint 10), so there is no way to cut a hole in the dial --
      # an aperture is drawn, not cut.
      #
      # Revised after rendering: a dark well with light text (the first
      # draft) read as a grey UI chip sitting on the dial, not a cut
      # through it -- a real date window shows a *light* wheel through a
      # *dark* dial plate, with the text dark-on-light on the wheel itself.
      # So this inverts the first draft: the well is `color.fg`
      # (the light wheel), the text on top of it is `color.bg`
      # (dark, so it reads against its own wheel rather than the dial), and
      # a `color.dark` frame -- the same role the two register
      # cards fill their own boxes with -- rings it for the bevel. That
      # frame colour, not `fg`, is deliberate: it has to read as a third,
      # distinct tone against a light (`fg`) well, which a same-colour
      # frame could not. Both windows sit on the vertical centre line,
      # day-of-week above the axle and day-of-month below it, as the
      # user asked -- well inside the numeral ring and
      # well clear of the shared register cards, which are off at dx
      # ±50%r.
      #
      # Both windows are wider than tall, not a tall, narrow "keycap":
      # day and date are both FONT_XTINY (below), so one line height
      # governs both boxes' height, and only the width differs -- wider
      # for "Wed"/"Mon" (day), narrower for a 1-2 digit date. A
      # convincing window shape matters more here than which of the two
      # reads bigger.
      day_window_well:
        type: rectangle
        at: { anchor: center, dy: -26%r }
        size: { width: 26%r, height: 20%r }
        corner_radius: 3%r
        color: color.track
      day_window_frame:
        type: rectangle
        at: { anchor: center, dy: -26%r }
        size: { width: 26%r, height: 20%r }
        corner_radius: 3%r
        filled: false
        thickness: 1px
        color: color.dark

      date_window_well:
        type: rectangle
        at: { anchor: center, dy: 26%r }
        size: { width: 22%r, height: 20%r }
        corner_radius: 3%r
        color: color.track
      date_window_frame:
        type: rectangle
        at: { anchor: center, dy: 26%r }
        size: { width: 22%r, height: 20%r }
        corner_radius: 3%r
        filled: false
        thickness: 1px
        color: color.dark

    elements:
      # The day/date readings themselves are data-bound, so they cannot
      # live in `static:` above (any data binding in a static subtree is
      # rejected outright -- docs/guide/elements.md "static:") -- only their wells
      # and frames can. Document order puts them after the wells/frames
      # (already drawn first, being static) and before the hands below, so
      # a real watch's own draw order falls out for free: hands are drawn
      # last and cross over the date windows, exactly like the real thing.
      # The format has no case-transform or letter-spacing
      # key, so `%a` draws exactly what the firmware's own localisation
      # returns (e.g. "Thu") rather than a forced, tracked "THU" -- noted
      # here rather than silently claimed otherwise.
      day_text:
        type: text
        text: "{date.today:%a}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: center, dy: -26%r }
        color: color.bg

      date_text:
        type: text
        text: "{date.today:%e}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: center, dy: 26%r }
        color: color.bg

      # No trailing "center pin" element here, unlike `analog`'s own
      # `center_pin` -- see `hand_sets: vintage:`'s own comment above for why:
      # `minute`'s hub circle plus `second`'s own pivot dot already cap the
      # joint, and a `color.bg` pin big enough to matter on these
      # thinner hands punched a hole through both instead of covering them.
      roman_hands:
        type: hands
        set: vintage
        at: { anchor: center }
        seconds: awake
        antialias: true
        lint:
          allow: [antialias-dither]
          reason: "a soft edge on the 64-colour MIP panel dithers; accepted
            so the rotated vintage hands do not stair-step -- the same
            acceptance the analog layout's own hands carry above"

sport.blurb: time, a heart-rate graph and four readouts, distance in the wearer's units
sport.text:
# A data-heavy digital face: the time, a heart-rate graph, and four
# icon-and-value readouts, with a battery bar at the bottom.
#
# Each readout is a `group`: a box of its own that its children are placed
# inside, so moving the group moves both. Holding a group opens the matching
# Garmin glance (`on_hold:`) -- the one gesture a live face gets.
#
# `activity.distance` arrives in centimetres; `units: auto` shows it in km or
# miles, whichever the wearer chose on the watch, and `{unit}` prints the
# label. Try `wfb preview <file> --units statute`.
#
# Every reading here can be absent (no heart-rate lock yet, a fresh day), so
# each says what to draw instead: `absent: "--"`.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"
    track: "#555555"
    hot: "#FF5500"
    accent: "#00AAFF"
    good: "#00FF00"
    low: "#FF0000"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

elements:
  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d %b}"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -66%r }
    color: color.dim

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_MEDIUM
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -38%r }
    color: color.fg

  # The last four hours of heart rate, time-binned on the watch. `wfb series`
  # lists the other series a face may plot.
  hr_graph:
    type: graph
    series: heart_rate
    range: 4h
    style: area
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -2%r }
    size: { width: 70%r, height: 22%r }
    min: auto
    max: auto
    color: color.hot
    on_hold: heart_rate

  hr:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -50%r, dy: 22%r }
    align: left
    on_hold: heart_rate
    children:
      hr_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: heart
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.hot
      hr_value:
        type: text
        text: "{heart_rate.current:d}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  steps:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 8%r, dy: 22%r }
    align: left
    on_hold: steps
    children:
      steps_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: steps
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.accent
      steps_value:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.steps / 1000.0:.1f}k"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  distance:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -50%r, dy: 42%r }
    align: left
    children:
      distance_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: distance
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.good
      distance_value:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.distance:.1f}{unit}"
        units: auto
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  calories:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 8%r, dy: 42%r }
    align: left
    on_hold: calories
    children:
      calories_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: flame
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.hot
      calories_value:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.calories:d}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  # A colour may read data: the bar turns red below 20%.
  battery:
    type: gauge
    style: bar
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 64%r }
    size: { width: 36%r, height: 5%r }
    color: "system.battery < 20 ? color.low : color.good"
    track_color: color.track
    on_hold: battery

themed.blurb: light/dark schemes, accent colours and two complication slots set on the watch
themed.text:
# A face the wearer restyles on the watch itself: a light or dark scheme, an
# accent colour, a data colour, and two complication slots whose content they
# pick -- all from the fēnix 8's own watch face editor, with no phone app.
#
# The editor has exactly four axes (docs/guide/configuration.md):
#
# * `style:` -- each entry names a `scheme:` from `theme:`, a set of roles
#   (`color.bg`, `.fg`, ...) that switch together;
# * `accent_color:` and `data_color:` -- one colour each, `color.accent`
#   and `color.data`;
# * `slots:` -- named complication slots, drawn by `type: data`.
#
# A watch without the editor (the Forerunner 955 is one) offers the same
# choices in a settings menu the build generates; one with neither keeps
# every `default:` forever, and the linter says so.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]

# Every channel is 0x00, 0x55, 0xAA or 0xFF, the colours a MIP panel shows
# without dithering -- including every choice offered below.
resources:
  palette:
    black: "#000000"
    white: "#FFFFFF"
    light_gray: "#AAAAAA"
    dark_gray: "#555555"
    orange: "#FF5500"
    amber: "#FFAA00"
    cyan: "#00FFFF"
    sky_blue: "#00AAFF"
    lime: "#AAFF00"

theme:
  schemes:
    dark:
      label: "Dark"
      colors: { bg: color.black, fg: color.white, dim: color.light_gray }
    light:
      label: "Light"
      colors: { bg: color.white, fg: color.black, dim: color.dark_gray }

config:
  style:
    default: dark
    choices:
      dark: { scheme: dark }
      light: { scheme: light }
  accent_color:
    default: color.orange
    choices: [color.orange, color.amber, color.cyan, color.lime]
  data_color:
    default: color.sky_blue
    choices: [color.sky_blue, color.white, color.amber]
  slots:
    top:
      default: body_battery
      choices: any # the editor's own full complication picker
    bottom:
      default: steps
      choices: [steps, heart_rate, calories]

static:
  # A config colour in `static:` is repainted when the wearer changes it.
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg
    # One allow anywhere accepts the single, face-wide warning.

  accent_ring:
    type: arc
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 94%r
    thickness: 4px
    start_angle: 0deg
    sweep: 360deg
    color: color.accent

elements:
  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -40%r }
    color: color.dim

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 6%r }
    color: color.fg

  # A slot draws the chosen complication's icon and reading. It takes no
  # format spec -- the reading's type depends on what the wearer picks.
  top_slot:
    type: data
    slot: top
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -66%r }
    font: FONT_SMALL
    icon: { size: 14%r, gap: 2%r, color: color.accent }
    color: color.data
    short: true # 7-character weather and training-status names
    absent: "--"
    on_hold: auto # opens the glance for whatever the slot shows

  bottom_slot:
    type: data
    slot: bottom
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 52%r }
    font: FONT_SMALL
    icon: { size: 14%r, gap: 2%r, color: color.accent }
    color: color.data
    absent: "--"
    on_hold: auto
